English_term: Treat the tip first in acute conditions
English_definition_description: A principle to address symptoms in acute conditions, for example, it is important to stop bleeding for heavy blood loss, to arrest diarrhoea for fulminant diarrhoea, alleviate pain for severe, intense pain and promote urination for urine retention.

English_term: Treat the root in remissive stages
English_definition_description: A principle to regulate and reinforce the body to address the root cause when medical conditions become stable.

English_term: Treat both the tip and root
English_definition_description: A principle to address both symptoms and root cause simultaneously when needed.
A principle to use an appropriate method and medicine according to seasonal climate changes.
A principle to use an appropriate method and medicine according to geographic features.
A principle to use an appropriate method and medicine according to individual gender, age and constitution.

English_term: Reinforce healthy qi to eliminate pathogenic factors
English_definition_description: A principle to reinforce anti-pathogenic qi to drive out the invading pathogenic factors. It is indicated for deficiency of anti-pathogenic qi coupled with exposure to pathogenic factors.

English_term: Reinforce healthy qi to strengthen the body
English_definition_description: A principle to reinforce anti-pathogenic qi to speed up recovery. It is indicated for deficiency of anti-pathogenic qi.

English_term: Eliminate pathogenic factors and reinforce healthy qi
English_definition_description: A principle to drive out the invading pathogenic factors, supplemented by reinforcing anti- pathogenic qi. It is indicated for excessive pathogenic factors with insufficiency of anti- pathogenic qi.

English_term: Reinforce healthy qi and remove pathogenic factors simultaneously
English_definition_description: A principle to reinforce anti-pathogenic qi and, at the same time, remove pathogenic factors. It is indicated for excessive pathogenic factors coupled with deficiency of healthy qi.

English_term: Remove pathogenic factors before reinforcing healthy qi
English_definition_description: A principle to remove the invading pathogenic factors, followed by reinforcing anti-pathogenic qi. It is indicated for deficiency of healthy qi coupled with acute conditions that require immediate removal of pathogenic factors.

English_term: Reinforce healthy qi before removing pathogenic factors
English_definition_description:
A principle to reinforce healthy qi, followed by removing the invading pathogenic factors. It is indicated for acute conditions that require
immediate removal of pathogneic factors coupled with deficiency of healthy qi.

A principle to use medicines opposite in nature to the disease, for example, to treat heat pattern with medicines cold in nature, treat cold pattern with medicine hot in nature, treat excess pattern with purgative/reducing medicines and treat deficiency pattern with tonic medicines.
A principle to treat cold conditions with medicines or formulas that are warm or hot in nature.
A principle to treat heat conditions with medicines or formulas that are cool or cold in nature.
A principle to treat deficiency conditions with tonic medicines or formulas.
A principle to treat excess conditions with medicines or formulas that are purgative or reducing in nature.

A principle to address false signs or symptoms   in extreme conditions such as extreme cold or heat. Under such conditions, it is necessary to use medicines similar in nature to the disease (i.e. follow the false symptoms), for example, to treat false heat with heat or treat false cold with cold.
A principle to treat false cold (true heat) symptoms with medicines cool or cold in nature.
A principle to treat false heat (true cold) symptoms with medicines warm or hot in nature.
A principle to treat food stagnation-related vomiting and diarrhoea or uterine bleeding due to blood stasis with purgative or stasis-unblocking medicines or formulas.

English_term: Regulate and balance yin and yang
English_definition_description: A principle to restore yin-yang equilibrium through medicines, food, emotions or reinforcing/ reducing needling techniques.

This is originally a needling method to puncture yin meridians for problems of yang meridians. Later, this method has been developed into a treatment principle based on interdependence between yin and yang: to add some yin-nourishing medicines to yang-reinforcing formulas to assist the transformation of yang qi.

This is originally a needling method to puncture yang meridians for problems of yin meridians. Later, this method has been developed into a principle based on interdependence between yin and yang: to add some yang-reinforcing medicines to yin-nourishing formulas to assist the generation of yin qi.

English_term: Reinforce the mother (element) for deficiency pattern
English_definition_description: A principle to treat deficiency of zang–fu organs based on the five-element theory. For example, since (spleen) earth promotes (lung) metal, lung deficiency can be treated by reinforcing the spleen and stomach.

English_term: Reduce the son (element) for excess pattern
English_definition_description: A principle to treat excess of zang–fu organs based on the five-element theory. For example, since (heart) fire promotes (spleen earth), hyperactivity of heart fire can be treated by reducing the spleen and stomach.
A principle to use same treatment for different diseases that share the same pathogenesis.

A principle to use different treatments for the same disease caused by different etiological factors; or a principle to treat the same disease according to differences in individuality,   time, geographic features, disease severity, differentiated patterns, and ongoing struggle between anti-pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors.

English_term: Treat the exterior before the interior
English_definition_description: A principle to treat an exterior pattern before an interior pattern. It applies to a severe exterior pattern but mild interior pattern in concurrent exterior and interior pattern. This principle aims to prevent pathogenic factors in the exterior from entering the interior.
Methods to release the exterior

Synonyms:
Promote sweating with pungent-warm_x000D_
Release the exterior and dissipate cold
English_definition_description: A treatment method to remove wind and dissipate cold with pungent, warm medicines or formulas. It is indicated for wind cold exterior pattern.
A treatment method to remove wind and clear heat with pungent, cool medicines or formulas. It is indicated for wind heat exterior pattern.

Synonyms: Release the exterior and clear heat
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear heat in the exterior. It is indicated for patterns involving both the Wei- defence and qi phases.

English_term: Remove pathogenic factors and release the exterior
Synonyms: Remove pathogenic factors in the exterior
English_definition_description: A method to remove pathogenic factors in the exterior. It is indicated for excess exterior pattern.

English_term: Remove wind and promote skin eruption
Synonyms: Release the exterior and promote skin eruption
English_definition_description: A treatment method to remove wind and promote skin eruption through formulas or external therapies. It is often indicated for measles or rubella.

English_term: Release the exterior and unblock meridians
English_definition_description: A treatment method to remove pathogenic  factors in the exterior and unblock meridian qi through formulas, tuina or external therapies. It is indicated for external pathogenic factors impairing the meridian qi.

English_term: Release the exterior and disperse the lung
English_definition_description: A treatment method to remove pathogenic factors in the exterior and disperse lung qi. It is indicated for wind warmth or wind cold attacking the lung.

English_term: Regulate and harmonize the ying nutrients and wei-defence
English_definition_description: A treatment method to coordinate between Ying nutrients and Wei-defence through removing wind and nourishing yin. It is indicated for disorders due to disharmony between the Ying nutrients and Wei-defence.

English_term: Eliminate dampness and release the exterior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to remove pathogenic factors in the exterior and resolve dampness with aroma. It is indicated for wind dampness affecting the exterior.

English_term: Regulate qi and release the exterior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to release the exterior and regulate qi. It is indicated for pathogenic factors affecting the exterior coupled with qi stagnation.

English_term: Reinforce healthy qi and release the exterior
English_definition_description:
A treatment method to release the exterior and reinforce the healthy qi. It is indicated for
deficiency of qi, blood, yin and yang coupled with external pathogenic factors affecting the exterior.

English_term: Supplement qi and release the exterior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to release the exterior and tonifyqi. It is indicated for exterior pattern coupled with qi deficiency.
Treatment methods to irritate the throat with medicine or tools to induce vomiting. The purpose is to expel harmful substances out of the body.

English_term: Induce vomiting to eliminate phlegm and salivation
English_definition_description: A treatment method to induce vomiting to eliminate phlegm. It is indicated for exuberant, turbid phlegm affecting the upper or middle jiao.

English_term: Induce vomiting to eliminate wind phlegm
English_definition_description: A treatment method to induce vomiting to eliminate wind phlegm. It is indicated for wind phlegm affecting the upper part of the body.

English_term: Induce sweating to eliminate retained phlegm and food
English_definition_description: A treatment method to induce vomiting to eliminate stagnant phlegm and food. It is indicated for phlegm intertwined with undigested food.

English_term: Induce vomiting to eliminate food retention
English_definition_description: A treatment method to induce vomiting to eliminate undigested food. It is indicated for food retention in the stomach.

English_term: Induce vomiting to refresh the mind
English_definition_description: A treatment method to induce vomiting to unblock and resuscitate. It is indicated for exuberant, turbid phlegm disturbing the heart mind.
Treatment methods to clear interior heat, retained water or stagnant blood.

Fire-clearing purgation_x000D_
Purgation with bitter-cold_x000D_
Drastic purgation

English_term: Promote bowel movements and circulate qi
English_definition_description:
A treatment method to combine purgative and qi-circulating medicines. It is indicated for
conditions due to constipation due to heat and qi stagnation.
A treatment method to combine purgative, yang- warming and cold-dissipating medicines. It is indicated for conditions due to excessive cold retention.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to combine purgative, fluid- generating and dryness-moistening medicines. It is indicated for constipation due to intestinal dryness or yin deficiency.

English_term: Benefit qi and promote bowel movements
Synonyms: Supplement qi and promote bowel movements
English_definition_description: A treatment method to supplement qi to promote bowel movements. It is indicated for constipation due to qi deficiency.

English_term: Warm yang and promote bowel movements
English_definition_description: A treatment method to combine purgative, yang- warming and cold-dissipating medicines. It is indicated for constipation due to (yang) deficiency cold.

English_term: Moisten the intestine and clear heat
English_definition_description: A treatment method to combine purgative, ying- nourishing, dryness-moistening and heat-clearing medicines. It is indicated for conditions due to heat retention and intestinal dryness.
A treatment method to use medicines to soften hardness and moisten dryness. It is indicated for conditions due to dryness resulting from fluid insufficiency.

English_term: Promote bowel movements and expel water
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use purgative medicines to resolve water retention. It is indicated for conditions due to internal retention of water fluid.
A treatment method to conduct urgent purgation to preserve yin fluids. It is indicated for febrile disease with dry heat consuming yin fluids.

English_term: Methods to release both the exterior and interior
Synonyms: Methods to concurrently release both exterior and interior
English_definition_description: Treatment methods to remove pathogenic factors in both the exterior and interior.

Chinese_synonyms: 发表攻里|发表攻下|解表攻下
English_term: Release the exterior and purge the interior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to combine purgative and exterior-releasing medicines. It is indicated for excess pattern involving both the exterior and interior.

English_term: Release the exterior and clear the interior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to combine exterior-releasing and interior-clearing medicines. It is indicated for exterior–interior heat pattern or exterior cold with interior heat pattern.

English_term: Release the exterior and warm the interior
Synonyms: Induce sweating and warm the interior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use medicines to induce sweating, release the exterior, warm the interior and dissipate cold. It is indicated for exterior- interior cold pattern or exterior heat with interior cold pattern.
Treatment methods to harmonize and release pathogenic factors affecting Shaoyang or coordinate functions of the zang–fu organs.

English_term: Harmonize and release the exterior and interior
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use medicines that are neutral in property to harmonize between the exterior and interior. It is indicated for mild conditions involving both the exterior and interior.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to soothe the liver, fortify the spleen and regulate qi activity to harmonize between the liver and spleen. It is indicated or liver qi stagnation with spleen deficiency or liver hyperactivity with spleen deficiency.

English_term: Soothe the liver and harmonize the stomach
English_definition_description: A treatment method to regulate qi activity of the liver and stomach to harmonize between the liver and stomach. It is indicated for conditions due to qi stagnation of the liver and stomach or disharmony between the liver and stomach.

English_term: Regulate and harmonize the stomach and intestines
Synonyms: Harmonize between the stomach and intestines
English_definition_description: A treatment method to regulate qi activity of the stomach and intestines to harmonize between the stomach and intestines. It is indicated for conditions due to qi stagnation of the stomach and intestines.

English_term: Regulate and harmonize the spleen and stomach
Synonyms: Harmonize between the spleen and stomach
English_definition_description: A treatment method to regulate qi activity of the spleen and stomach to harmonize between the spleen and stomach. It is indicated for conditions due to disharmony between the spleen and stomach.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to use qi-regulating and blood-circulating formulas. It is indicated for conditions due to disharmony between qi and blood.

English_term: Regulate qi and harmonize the ying nutrients
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use medicines to regulate qi and harmonize the Ying nutrients. It is indicated for conditions due to disharmony between qi and Ying nutrients.

English_term: Balance and regulate cold and heat
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use neutral-property medicines to clear heat and remove cold. It is indicated for conditions due to disharmony between (yin) cold and (yang) heat.

English_term: Induce urination and promote bowel movements
English_definition_description: A treatment method to induce urination and promote bowel movements to eliminate pathogenic factors.

English_term: Induce vomiting and promoting bladder/ bowel movements
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use medicines to induce vomiting, eliminate phlegm and promote bladder or bowel movements to separately eliminate pathogenic factors.

English_term: Release the exterior and clear interior excess
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use medicines to release the exterior and clear interior excess to separately eliminate pathogenic factors from the exterior and interior.

Synonyms: Regulate and nourish the Chong and Ren
English_definition_description: A treatment method to use formulas to regulate qi and blood of the Chong and Ren. It is indicated for conditions due to disharmony between the Chong and Ren.

English_term: Clear heat in the ying nutrients and cool blood
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear heat in the Ying nutrients and cool blood. It is indicated for conditions due to heat entering the Ying nutrients and blood.

A treatment method to clear heat of the zang–fu organs. It is indicated for excess heat in the zang– fu organs.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear the heart and reduce fire. It is indicated for conditions due to exuberance of heart fire.
A treatment method to clear lung heat. It is indicated for conditions due to exuberance of lung heat.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat of the spleen and stomach. It is indicated for excess heat in the spleen and stomach.

Chinese_synonyms: 清肝泻火|清肝泻热|清肝泄热

English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the liver meridian. It is indicated for fire hyperactivity along the liver meridian, exuberance of liver fire and upward flaming of liver fire.
A treatment method to clear fire heat in the gallbladder meridian. It is indicated for stagnant heat in the gallbladder meridian.

English_term: Clear heat in the liver and gallbladder
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the liver and gallbladder. It is indicated for fire hyperactivity of the liver and gallbladder.

English_term: Clear heat in the heart and spleen
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the heart and spleen. It is indicated for heat accumulating in the heart and spleen.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the heart and liver. It is indicated for fire hyperactivity of the heart and liver.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the heart and lung. It is indicated for exuberant heat in the heart and lung.

English_term: Clear heat in the heart and kidney
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the heart and kidney. It is indicated for fire heat in the heart and kidney.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat in the liver and stomach. It is indicated for liver fire attacking the stomach or exuberant heat in the liver and stomach.

A treatment method to clear fire heat in the urinary bladder. It is indicated for heat strangury or retained heat in the urinary bladder.

English_term: Clear heat and quiet the fetus
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear fire heat to quiet the fetus. It is indicated for threatened abortion due to heat disturbing the uterus.

English_term: Clear heat and relieve bone-steaming sensation
English_definition_description: A treatment method to clear heat, reduce fire and eliminate bone-steaming sensation. It is indicated for conditions due to deficiency fire or bone- steaming sensation.

English_definition_description: A treatment method to warm and reinforce yang qi to dissipate yin cold. It is indicated for yin cold due to yang deficiency.

A treatment method to reinforce kidney yang  and combine medicines that enter meridians to astringe floating yang qi, i.e. to guide kidney yang into kidney yin. It is indicated for decline of vital fire or floating of deficiency yang.

English_term:
Harmonize the ying nutrients and_x000D_
regenerate new tissues
English_definition_description: A treatment method to harmonize between   the Ying nutrients and blood, circulate blood, regenerate new blood and flesh, and speed up wound healing. It is indicated for delayed wound healing due to blood stagnation.

English_term: Disperse and unblock the three jiao
English_definition_description: A treatment method to regulate qi, eliminate pathogenic factors and unblock the three jiao. It is indicated for pathogenic factors impairing the qi flow of the three jiao.

A treatment method to nourish kidney yin, astringe kidney yang, reduce heart fire and calm the heart mind to submerge yang and coordinate between the heart and kidney. It is indicated for conditions due to disharmony between the heart fire and kidney water.

A treatment method to clear heat, reduce fire, submerge yang and clear the head and eyes. It is indicated for headache, eye pain and dizziness due to upward flaming of fire heat or hyperactivity of yang qi.
A treatment method to lubricate and unblock orifices. It is indicated for dry orifices due to insufficiency of yin fluids.

English_term: Open the chest and sooth the diaphragm
English_definition_description: A treatment method to eliminate pathogenic factors, regulate qi, lift yang, and down-regulate turbidity to soothe the chest and diaphragm. It is indicated for chest stuffiness, distension, fullness and tightness.
A treatment method to use tuina or other therapies to repair the broken sinews or bones. It is indicated for sinew or bone injuries.
A treatment method to strengthen the sinews or bones through exercise or taking medicine. It is indicated for weak sinews/bones due to heredity, trauma or chronic diseases.
A treatment method to eliminate phlegm, regulate qi, break stasis and unblock collaterals to soften hardness, disperses nodules and resolve masses. It is indicated for masses, lumps or swelling.

A treatment method to disperse the lung (metal) and inhibit the liver (wood). It is indicated for migratory pain in the subcostal region, cough or panting due to hyperactivity of liver yang and failure of lung qi to disperse and descend.

A treatment method to warm and reinforce the vital fire to supplement the transportation and transformation of the spleen (earth). It is indicated for early morning diarrhoea due to decline of the vital fire and spleen yang deficiency.

English_term: Mutual generation between metal and water
English_definition_description: A treatment method to tonify the kidney and nourish the lung for lung deficiency and kidney deficiency, since the lung (metal) and kidney (water) mutually support physiologically and mutually affect pathologically.
A treatment method to tonify the spleen (earth) to restrain overflow of water dampness. It is indicated for oedema or diarrhoea due to spleen deficiency.

English_term: Reduce the south to reinforce the north
English_definition_description: A treatment method to reduce heart fire and reinforce kidney water. The south here refers to heart fire, whereas the north refers to kidney water.
All causes of diseases.

English_term: To differentiate pattern to reveal an etiology
English_definition_description: A method to seek the etiological factors according to clinical manifestations.
A theory that classifies etiological factors into internal, external and neither internal nor external.
These mainly refer to seven emotional disturbances.
These mainly refer to six exogenous pathogenic factors.

English_term: Neither internal nor external etiological factors
English_definition_description: Pathogenic factors that are not categorized as external or internal, such as improper diet, over- exertion, traumatic injuries, animal/insect bites, drowning etc.
Pathogenic factors that attack the body through the skin, mouth and nose, including six pathogenic factors and epidemic qi.
Internal dysfunctions due to extreme emotions, over-exertion, and improper diet.
Opposite to healthy qi, it is a collective term for all pathogenic factors.
Opposite to yin pathogens, refers to pathogenic factors of yang nature, such as wind, summer-heat or fire-heat.
Opposite to yang pathogens, refers to pathogenic factors of yin nature, such as cold or dampness.

Opposite to excess pathogens, it is a collective term for exogenous pathogenic factors that invade the body when the body is weak. Alternatively,
it refers to pathogenic qi that transmits from the mother organ to the son organ.
Opposite to deficiency pathogens, it is a collective term for pathogenic factors. Alternatively, it refers to pathogenic qi that transmits from the son organ to the mother organ.
A collective term for epidemic, etiological factors associated with the four seasons.
External pathogenic factors that damage the human body.
A collective term for six exogenous pathogenic factors: wind, cold, summer-heat, dampness, dryness and fire.
A collective term for exogenous pathogenic factors with high contagiousness.
A pathogenic factor with high contagiousness.
Seven normal emotions include joy, anger, anxiety, overthinking, grief, fear and fright.
A collective term for damage caused by extreme emotions including joy, anger, anxiety, overthinking, grief, fear and fright.
Fire pattern transformed from disturbance of joy, anger, grief, overthinking and fear.
Diet harmful to health, including unhealthy dietary habits, ingestion of contaminated food, dietary preference, etc.
A collective term for over-exertion and physical inactivity.
A pathogenic factor that induces or aggravates medical conditions by errors of health care professionals.
Harm to the body by animals or insects.
A pathogenic factor characterized by opening the skin pores, high mobility and upward/outward movement.
Wind loosens the interspace between skin/muscle fibers and opens the skin pores, resulting in sweating and aversion to wind.
Wind is characterized by upward flowing. It easily affects the head, face, surface of the body and yang meridians.
Wind is characterized by constant moving. It causes the limbs to tremble.
Wind is characterised by swift changes. Diseases caused by wind are marked by a sudden onset of symptoms in moving locations.

Pinyin_term: fēng wéi bǎi bìng zhī zhǎng
English_term: Wind is the leading cause of diseases
Synonyms: Wind is the spearhead of a hundred diseases
English_definition_description: Wind may cause a wide variety of conditions. It is the spearhead of exogenous pathogenic factors and liable to associate itself with cold, dampness, dryness and heat.
A pathogenic factor characterized by coldness, stagnation, congealing and contraction.
Cold is yin in nature and can easily impair yang qi.
Pathogenic cold causes qi/blood to stagnate, blocks meridians, and causes pain.
Pathogenic cold constricts qi, blocks the skin pores, and causes contractions.
A pathogenic factor commonly seen between the summer solstice and beginning of autumn. It is characterized by flames ascending and dispersing.
Pathogenic summer heat is characterized by extreme hotness. Often causes hyperactive yang heat.
Summer heat ascends and disperses. Often directly affects the qi phase, opens the sweating pores and damages body fluids.

English_term: Summer heat often combines with dampness
English_definition_description: Summer is hot, humid and rainy. The summer heat provokes dampness and is often liable to mix itself with dampness.
A pathogenic factor that obstructs the flow of qi. It is characterized by heaviness, turbidity, stickiness and downward flowing.
Dampness is a tangible pathogenic factor and is easy to obstruct qi movement.
Dampness is yin in nature and can easily damage yang qi. It is tangible and can obstruct the flow of yang qi.
Pathogenic dampness is characterized by its heaviness and turbidity. The diseases caused by it may lead to heaviness of the body and turbidity of secretions and excrements.
Dampness is characterized by stickiness and stagnation. It causes sticky, viscous secretions and discharges. Dampness-induced conditions often last a long time.
Dampness move downward and affects the yin and lower parts of the body.
A pathogenic factor that consumes body fluids and tends to damage the lung.
Dryness desiccates by consuming body fluids and causing body fluid deficiency and lack of moisture.
Dryness invades the body through the nose, mouth and skin pores. It easily damages the lung fluids and impairs the dispersing of lung qi.
A pathogenic factor that flames upward, consumes qi and body fluids, engenders wind, stirs blood, and harasses the heart spirit.
A pathogenic factor that causes excessive pathological changes of hot and yang nature.
A collective term for pathogenic warm heat, including spring warmth, wind warmth, summer heat warmth, damp warmth, autumn dryness, winter warmth, pestilence warmth, warm toxin, warm malaria, etc.
Toxic pathogens include toxins transformed from six exogenous pathogenic factors, toxic fire from sores/ulcers, toxic heat, snake venom, rabies or toxic lacquer.
The nature of pathogenic fire flames upward. It causes heat symptoms and often affects the upper part of the body.
Fire tends to stir liver wind. Extreme heat can cause stirring of wind.
Since fire may burn the vessels and collaterals and cause the blood to move recklessly, it often results in bleeding or macular eruption.

English_term: Fire consumes qi and body fluids
English_definition_description: Since fire consumes healthy qi and scorches yin fluids, it often causes deficiency of both qi and thin fluids.

English_term: Fire tends to disturb the heart spirit
Synonyms: Fire tends to disturb the heart Shen
English_definition_description: Since fire tends to disturb the heart spirit, it often causes mental restlessness.
Since fire heat tends to enter the blood and remain in a fixed location, it often causes sores/ ulcers.
Hyperactive, pathogenic fire that consumes healthy qi.
Excessive anger damages liver qi, impairs the function of liver in maintaining the free flow of qi, causes the qi to rise, and results in disordered qi and blood.
Excessive joy damages heart spirit, consumes heart qi and results in mental derangement.
Excessive overthinking damages spleen qi, causes qi to stagnate, and impairs the function of the spleen in transportation and transformation.
Excessive grief damages and consumes lung qi and impairs the dispersal of lung qi.
Excessive fear damages kidney qi, causes kidney qi to descend, and impairs the function of the kidney in storing essence.
Improper diet, including excessive hunger and binge eating.
Intake of contaminated or poisonous food.
Excessive indulgence in specific food, including cold or hot food, certain flavours or alcohol.
The five flavours are spicy, sweet, sour, bitter and salty. Habitual preference for a particular flavour or taste may bring about adverse reactions or damage the five zang organs.
Overwork can be physical, mental or sexual.
Excessive physical activities damage the zang–fu organs and cause qi deficiency of the zang organs.
Excessive mental activities tend to damage heart blood and spleen qi.
Excessive sexual activities consume and damage kidney essence.
Physical inactivity leads to imbalances in the flow of qi and blood, weak tendons and bones, stagnant qi of the spleen and stomach. In severe cases, it may even cause other secondary diseases.

The five exhaustions are listed as follows: Long- time observation damages blood; long-time lying damages qi; long-time sitting damages muscles; long-time standing damages bones; and long-time walking damages sinews. Alternatively, the five overstrains refer to deficiencies of the five zang organs (i.e. liver, heart, spleen, lung and kidney).
A collective term for stagnation of qi, blood, phlegm, fire, food and dampness. Often results from qi stagnation of the liver and spleen.

Refers to the seven pathogenic factors that lead to deficiency and consumption, including improper diet, anxiety, drink, sex, hunger, over-exertion, and damage to meridians, collaterals, Ying-nutrients, Wei-defense and qi.
Tangible phlegm is visible, touchable and audible when it is secreted from the airways.
Intangible phlegm is invisible and impalpable; however, it can cause pathogenic features of phlegm.

The spleen governs transportation and transformation of water and food. The failure of the spleen to transport and transform water fluids may cause internal retention of water dampness and generate phlegm.
The lung dominates water and regulates the water passage. The failure of the lung to disperse qi may cause internal retention of phlegm fluids.
Fluid retention that lasts a long period of time. It is one type of fluid retention.
A type of fluid retention that is deeply located and hard to remove.
A pathological product formed during slow blood flow or as blood coagulates. It is also a secondary pathogenic factor.
The gravel-like substance that accumulates in the human body, especially in the ducts and cavities of zang–fu organs. It is also a secondary pathogenic factor.
An inherited etiological factor that transmits the body constitution and disease of the mother to her fetus.
A pre-birth toxin. It is a pathogenic factor that causes infantile skin rashes.
A collective term for a congenitally weak constitution and a deficiency of qi and blood. It is a major contributing factor to a deficiency of healthy qi.
Congenital constitutional weakness is an internal etiological factor of healthy qi deficiency.
The five pathological states of wind, fire, cold, dryness and dampness due to dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs.

Opposite to external wind, it is a pathological state of yang qi hyperactivity and wind stirring due to disordered qi and blood of the zang–fu organs.
This includes extreme heat generating wind, liver yang transforming into wind, blood deficiency generating wind and yin deficiency stirring wind.
Opposite to external cold, it is a pathological state of deficiency cold due to yang qi deficiency of the zang–fu organs.
Opposite to external dampness, it is a pathological state of retained water, dampness, phlegm and turbidity due to dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs and disordered water metabolism.
Opposite to external dryness, it is a pathological state of body fluids failing to moisten the body.
Opposite to external fire, it is a pathological state of fire heat due to disordered qi, blood, yin and yang of the zang–fu organs.
The pathogenic fire produced from improper diet, fatigue, joy, anger, grief, overthinking, qi deficiency or yang deficiency.
The mechanism of the occurrence, progress, and change of the disease.

Opposite to pathogenic factors, it is a collective term for physiological functions of the body, including the body’s ability to adapt to the external environment, defend against pathogens and recover from diseases.
Opposite to the latent pathogenic qi in the theory of warm disease, it often causes a sudden onset of disease.
Opposite to exposure to acute pathogenic qi in the theory of febrile diseases, it causes the occurrence of diseases after a period of time.
A rapid appearance of symptoms after being in contact with a pathogen.
A gradual appearance of symptoms after being in contact with a pathogen.
Relapse of diseases due to etiological or inducing factors.
Relapse of diseases due to intake of improper diet or intake of contaminated food.
Relapse of disease due to the damage to healthy qi by overwork
A pathological state of pathogenic factors affecting two meridians that are interior–exteriorly connected.
Transmission and transformation of diseases among five zang organs.
Two or more external pathogenic factors invade the body. Alternatively, it means exogenous pathogenic factors triggering previously existing diseases.
Pathological states caused by pathogenic factors invading the mouth, nose, ears and eyes.

English_term: Struggle between anti- pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors
English_definition_description: The struggle between healthy qi and pathogenic factors determines the pathogenic nature of diseases. Alternatively, it is specifically used to explain the pathogenesis of alternating fever and chills in Shaoyang disease due to cold damage.

English_term: Waxing and waning of anti-pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors
English_definition_description: The pathological states due to the struggle between healthy qi and pathogenic factors.
A pathological state due to deficiency of healthy qi and excess of pathogenic factors. This includes deficiency complicated with excess and excess complicated with deficiency.
A pathological state that mainly manifests as a deficiency of healthy qi, accompanied by excessive pathogenic factors.
A pathological state that mainly manifests as excess of pathogenic factors, accompanied by a deficiency of healthy qi.

English_term: True or false deficiency and excess
English_definition_description: The false symptoms contrary to the true nature of the disease. This includes true deficiency with false excess and true excess with false deficiency.
The false excess symptoms due to extreme deficiency of healthy qi.
The false deficiency symptoms due to extreme excess of pathogenic factors.
The mutual transformation between deficiency of healthy qi and excess of pathogenic factors. This includes excess transforming into deficiency and deficiency into excess.
A transformation from an excess pattern (hyperactivity of pathogenic factors) to a deficiency pattern (deficiency of healthy qi).
A transformation from a deficiency pattern (deficiency of healthy qi) to an excess pattern (hyperactivity of pathogenic factors).

A general term for pathological states due to waxing and waning of yin and yang. This includes excess of yin or yang, deficiency of yin or yang, mutual impairment between yin and yang, rejection between yin and yang, transformation between yin and yang, and depletion/loss of yin or yang.
Pathological states due to excess of yin or yang.
Coexisting yin waxing and yang waning. Over time, excess yin cold may damage yang qi and result in yang depletion.
Mutual restraint between yin and yang maintains relative yin–yang equilibrium. The failure of yang to restrain yin may cause relative yin excess.
Coexisting yang waxing and yin waning. Often develops when waxing yang severely damages yin; however, yin damage is more severe.

English_term: When yang prevails, yin fluids will be consumed.
English_definition_description: A pathological state of overwhelming yang heat consuming yin fluids.
A pathological state of overwhelming yang leading to excess heat.

English_term: When yin prevails, yang qi will be impaired.
English_definition_description: A pathological state of excess yin cold consuming yang qi.
A pathological state of overwhelming yin leading to excess cold.
Pathological states due to deficiency of yin or yang.
A pathological state of yang qi deficiency leading to deficiency cold.
A pathological state in which yin fluid fails to control yang and causes a relative hyperactivity of yang and deficiency heat.

English_term: Yin deficiency leading to yang hyperactivity
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which yin fluid fails to control yang and causes a relative hyperactivity of yang.

English_term: Yin deficiency leading to fire hyperactivity
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which yin fluid fails to control yang and causes a relative hyperactivity of yang and deficiency fire.

English_term: Mutual impairment between yin and yang
English_definition_description: A pathological state of deficiency of both yin and yang. Often results from severe deficiency of yin affecting yang or vice versa. This includes yin deficiency affecting yang and yang deficiency affecting yin.

A pathological state in which yang qi deficiency impedes the generation of yin, resulting
in deficiency of both yin and yang with a preponderance of yang deficiency.
A pathological state in which consumption of yin affects yang qi, resulting in deficiency of both yin and yang with a preponderance of yin deficiency.

English_term: Dual deficiency of yin and yang
English_definition_description: A pathological state of coexisting yin deficiency and yang deficiency.

A serious pathological state in which extremely excessive yin in the interior forces the deficient yang to spread outward or extremely excessive yang in the interior keeps deficient yin on the outside, forming pseudo-heat or pseudo-cold. This includes excessive yin rejecting yang and excessive yang rejecting yin.
A pathological state of true cold with false heat when interior yin cold due to extreme yang deficiency forces the deficient yang to float on the exterior of the body.
A pathological state of true heat with false cold when interior yang heat blocks the movement of qi and forces the yin to float on the exterior of the body.
A pathological state of upward floating of yang qi due to excessive yin rejecting yang or loss/ consumption of essence blood.
A critical state of sudden, heavy loss of yin fluid or yang qi. This includes yin collapse and yang collapse.
A critical state of massive loss and sudden failure of yin fluid.
A critical state of massive loss and sudden failure of yang qi.
A pathological state of exhaustion of yin fluid and loss of yang qi.
A critical state of separation between yin and yang due to extreme deficiency of yin and yang.
Disordered activity of qi in ascending, descending, entering and exiting. It may cause qi stagnation, adverse qi flow, qi sinking, qi blockage and qi exhaustion.

A general term for dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs. It is often used to explain dysfunctions of qi of the zang–fu organs in ascending the clear and descending the turbid. It may cause hiccups, chest stuffiness, abdominal distension/pain and irregular bowel/bladder movements.
A pathological state of decreased zang–fu functions or body weakness due to deficiency of qi.
A pathological state in which extreme deficiency of qi causes qi to float on the exterior of the body.
A pathological state in which qi is obstructed inside.
A pathological state of reversed upflow of qi. Either excessive upward flow of qi or inhibited downward flow of qi.
A pathological state in which qi fails to lift or hold but flows downward.
A pathological state in which the movement of qi is inhibited.
Stagnant movement of qi. It is often associated with emotions and disorder of qi and blood. Often refers to liver qi stagnation.
A pathological state of prolonged qi stagnation transforming into fire heat.
A pathological state in which deficient blood fails to nourish the zang–fu organs and meridians/ channels.
A pathological state of slow, coagulated or stagnant circulation of blood.
A pathological state in which cold enters the blood phase and causes the blood to stagnate or coagulate.
A pathological state in which heat enters the blood phase and causes the blood to move recklessly.

English_term: Blood failing to flow within the vessels
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which blood moves recklessly out of the vessels.

English_term: Blood failing to nourish the sinews
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which liver blood fails to nourish the sinews and causes muscle/tendon spasm.
Any failure in the mutually coordinating relationship between qi and blood.

English_term: Dual deficiency of qi and blood
English_definition_description:
A pathological state of malnourishment of the body or weakened bodily function due to
simultaneous presence of qi deficiency and blood deficiency.
A pathological state in which the dysfunction of qi affects the blood and causes blood deficiency, stagnant blood or bleeding.

English_term: Reckless flow of blood due to heat
English_definition_description: A pathological state of bleeding due to heat in the blood stirring or consuming blood and forcing it out of the vessels.

English_term: Qi collapse following loss of thick fluids
English_definition_description: A critical state in which a massive loss of bodily fluids causes sudden collapse/loss of yang qi.

English_term: Qi failing to transform thin fluids
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which yang qi fails to vaporize water and perform qi transformation.

English_term: Water retention obstructing the flow of qi
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which retained water within the body impedes the qi ascending, descending and transformation of the zang–fu organs.

English_term: Blood stasis due to qi stagnation
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which stagnant qi affects the circulation of blood and causes simultaneous presence of qi stagnation and blood stasis.

English_term: Blood stasis due to qi deficiency
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which qi fails to promote the circulation of blood and causes blood stasis, resulting in simultaneous presence of qi deficiency and blood stasis.
A pathological state in which qi fails to contain blood and allows the blood to flow out of the vessels.

English_term: Qi collapse following heavy blood loss
English_definition_description: A critical state in which massive blood loss causes sudden collapse of qi.
A pathological state in which upward adverse flow of qi leads to blood rushing upward and results in haematemesis, haemoptysis or stroke.
A pathological state in which the thin, clear fluids are consumed.

A pathological state of emaciation and functional failures of the zang–fu organs. Alternatively,
it can be a life-threatening sign due to major consumption of heavy, thick fluids.

English_term: Fluid exhaustion leading to blood dryness
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which fluids fail to supplement blood and causes blood dryness and internal dry heat.

English_term: Dual deficiency of qi and yin
English_definition_description: A pathological state of simultaneous presence of qi deficiency and yin deficiency.

English_term: The water gate failing to operate
English_definition_description: A pathological state in which dysfunctions of the kidney in qi transformation causes inhibited urination (dysuria) and oedema.

A pathological state of yin–yang disharmony and hyperactive yang transforming into fire. Alternatively, it occurs when prolonged intake of pungent, warm-property aphrodisiacs generates internal fire toxins and consumes essence qi.

English_term: Disharmony between the Ying-nutrients and Wei-defence
English_definition_description: A pathological state of lack of coordination between the Ying-nutritive qi and Wei-defensive qi.
A pathological state of spontaneous sweating without fever due to deficiency of the Wei- defensive qi (in an exterior pattern).
A pathological state of sweating that occurs only during fever in an exterior pattern.

Synonyms: Frenetic stirring of the ministerial fire
English_definition_description: A pathological state of upward flame of fire due to yin deficiency of the liver and kidney. Common symptoms may include dizziness, headache, blurred vision, tinnitus, deafness, irritability, dream-disturbed sleep, feverish sensations in the palms, soles and chest, hypersexuality, nocturnal emissions, premature ejaculations, etc.

English_term: Patterns according to the eight principles

English_definition_description: Causes outward, upward symptoms and manifests as conditions characterized by excitability, hyperactivity, restlessness, and brightness. It encompasses exterior pattern, heat pattern and excess pattern.

Causes inward, downward symptoms and manifests as conditions characterized by inhibition, listlessness, tranquillity and gloominess. It encompasses interior pattern, cold pattern and deficiency pattern.

Characterized by fever, a red face, thirst, constipation and yellow or red urine. Alternatively, malar flush, night sweats, feverish sensations
in the palms, soles and chest, a dry, red tongue and a thready, rapid pulse may be present. It is sub-categorized into patterns of exterior heat, interior heat, deficiency heat and excess heat. Often results from contracting pathogenic heat or hyperactivity of yang due to yin deficiency.

Characterized by aversion to cold, cold intolerance, cold pain with preference for warmth, absence
of thirst, thin, clear phlegm and nasal discharge, clear, profuse urine, loose stools and a pale complexion. The tongue is purple with a white coating. The pulse is tight or slow. Often results from excess of yin qi or cold attacking the interior.

Characterized by high fever, thirst, chest tightness, panting, rapid breathing, phlegm sounds in
the throat, restlessness, delirium, abdominal distension/pain/tenderness, and scanty, dark- yellow urine or hesitant, painful urination. The tongue is rough with a dry, yellow coating. The pulse is replete and forceful. Contributing factors may include six pathogenic factors, parasites or dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs (subsequent food stagnation, retention of phlegm/fluid/water/ dampness and blood stasis).
Characterized by general weakness, a weak pulse and abdominal softness. Often results from insufficiency of qi, yin, yang or blood.

Characterized by aversion to wind/cold, fever, headache, and body aches. The tongue coating is thin. The pulse is floating. These signs and symptoms are often seen in the early stage
of externally contracted conditions that have a sudden onset, superficial location and a short duration. Often occurs when exogenous
pathogenic factors affect the interstices, joints and head.

A group of patterns caused by entering of external pathogens into the interior, improper diet, over exhaustion, emotional disturbance or phlegm stasis, resulting in disorders and dysfunctions in qi, blood, yin, yang, zang–fu organs and meridian systems.

English_term: True cold with false heat pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by true-cold signs and symptoms such as cold hands/feet, profuse, clear urine, a pale tongue with a white coating, coupled with false-heat signs and symptoms such as fever but with a desire to put on more clothes, flushed cheeks and thirst with a desire for hot water. Often results from blockage of external yang by severe interior yin and cold.
Characterized by simultaneous occurrence of cold pattern and heat pattern in one individual patient at a certain pathological stage.

English_term: True excess with false deficiency pattern
English_definition_description: An excess pattern that displays false deficiency symptoms.

English_term: Exterior cold with interior heat pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by aversion to cold, fever, body aches, absence of sweating, vexation, panting, and thirst. The tongue is red with a yellow, white coating. The pulse is floating and rapid. Often occurs when pathogenic cold binds the exterior and blocks the heat inside.

English_term: Exterior heat with interior cold pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by aversion to cold, fever, sweating, headache, sore throat, clear urine, loose stools, and abdominal fullness and distension. Often caused by constitutional yang deficiency coupled with contraction of external heat.

Characterized by aversion to cold, cold limbs, headache, body aches, and absence of sweating. Alternatively, coughing with white phlegm, cold pain in the stomach and abdomen, vomiting and diarrhoea with clear and watery discharge may also be present. Often occurs when pathogenic cold affects both the exterior and interior.

Characterized by fever, mild aversion to wind/cold, headache, body aches, vexation, panting, thirst, constipation and yellow urine. The tongue is red with a thin, yellow coating. The pulse is floating and rapid. Often occurs when pathogenic wind heat or pestilence affects both the exterior and interior.

English_term: Upper excess with lower deficiency pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by deficiency of the liver and kidney coupled with accumulation of phlegm heat in the upper body.

English_term: Upper heat with lower cold pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by heat retention in the upper body but cold retention in the lower body.

English_term: Upper cold with lower heat pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by cold retention in the upper body but heat retention in the lower body.

Synonyms: Half exterior and half interior (commonly used but wrong in meaning)
English_definition_description: Characterized by alternating fever and aversion to cold, fullness in the chest and sub-costal area, vexation, vomiting, poor appetite, a bitter mouth, a dry throat and blurred vision. The pulse is wiry. Often occurs when anti-pathogenic qi fights with pathogenic factors between the exterior and interior: exogenous pathogenic factors have not entered the interior or internal pathogenic factors have not reached the exterior.

Characterized by fever, aversion to heat, absence of sweating, headache, neck stiffness, restlessness, abdominal distension and constipation. In severe cases, mania may be present. The tongue coating is dry and thick. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often results from unresolved pathogenic factors in the exterior coupled with internal retention of undigested food, accumulated heat, phlegm fluid, water dampness, stagnant blood, dry faeces, pus, parasites and stones.

English_term: Exterior excess with interior deficiency pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by aversion to cold, absence of sweating, and fever. Associated symptoms include lassitude, shortness of breath, a poor appetite, fatigue, palpitations and lower back pain. The tongue is pale with a white coating. The pulse is superficial. Often occurs as a result of the struggle between anti-pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors coupled with deficiency of anti-pathogenic qi. Alternatively, it may result from deficiency of the heart, spleen and kidney coupled with external contraction of wind cold. It may also result from inappropriate use of purgative therapy for external contraction of wind cold.

English_term: Exterior deficiency with interior excess pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by aversion to wind, sweating, coughing with profuse phlegm, and abdominal distension/pain with tenderness, and constipation. The tongue is dark with a yellow, thick coating. Often results from deficiency of Wei-defensive qi coupled with build up of internal heat. Alternatively, it may occur when retained food in the stomach and intestines transform into heat, along with external contraction of wind. It may also result from inappropriate treatment
of an exterior pattern or inappropriate use of sweating therapy for an interior excess pattern.

Characterized by aversion to cold, fever, absence of sweating, headache and body aches. The pulse is superficial and tense. Often occurs when the struggle between yang qi and pathogenic factors closes the skin striae.

Characterized by coexistence of excess of pathogenic factors and deficiency of anti- pathogenic qi. It may present as a deficiency pattern coupled with excess, an excess pattern coupled with deficiency, or mixed deficiency and excess.

Chinese_synonyms: 风邪犯表证|风邪外袭证
English_definition_description: Characterized by aversion to wind, fever, sweating and a superficial pulse. Alternatively, skin itching, oedema, cough, sore throat, headache or body aches may be present. Often occurs when wind attacks the surface of the body and affects the normal functioning of the Wei-defence.

Chinese_synonyms: 风热外侵证|风热犯表证
Synonyms: Wind heat invading the exterior pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by fever, mild aversion to cold/wind, sweating, thirst, and red, sore throat. The tongue tip is red with a thin, yellow coating. The pulse
is superficial and rapid. Often occurs when wind heat attacks the surface of the body and affects the normal functioning of the Wei-defence.

Characterized by fever, thirst with little water intake, and limb heaviness. Alternatively, skin rashes, blisters, itching or oozing may be present. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating.
Often occurs when wind heat that carries dampness affects the skin.

Characterized by limb soreness/heaviness, and joint swelling, pain and impaired movement. Alternatively, skin itching, oozing, fever, and thirst may be present. The tongue is red with a dry, yellow/white coating. Often occurs when retained wind dampness transforms into heat.

Characterized by aversion to cold, fever, headache, body ache and joint soreness/pain. Associated symptoms include cough with thick phlegm, and  a sore/scratchy throat. The tongue tip is red with a dry, yellow/white coating. The pulse is rapid. Often occurs when retained wind cold transforms into heat and enters the interior.

Chinese_synonyms: 寒邪束表证|风寒束表证
Synonyms: Cold/wind cold binding the exterior pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by severe aversion to cold, fever, absence of sweating, headache, and body aches. Alternatively, nasal obstruction, clear nasal discharge, and cough may be present. The tongue coating is thin and white. The pulse is superficial and tense. Often occurs when wind cold blocks the skin pores.

English_term: Wind dampness attacking the exterior pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by body soreness/heaviness, headache with a heavy sensation, aversion to cold, fever that cannot be resolved by sweating, chest tightness, and absence of thirst. The tongue coating is white, slippery or greasy. The pulse
is soft and delayed. Often occurs when wind dampness attacks the surface of the body and obstructs the flow of Wei-defensive qi.

English_term: Wind toxin attacking the exterior pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by sudden skin itching, papules or wheals. The pulse is superficial. Often occurs when wind toxin attacks the surface of the body.

Characterized by sudden skin swelling, numbness, itching or pain and redness, swelling and pain of the head/face/mouth/nose and eyes. Alternatively, wheals may be present. The pulse is superficial and rapid. Often occurs when wind toxin attacks the skin.

English_term: Wind dampness accumulating in the skin pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by skin itching, ulceration, rashes or oozing. Often occurs when wind dampness retains in the skin.

English_term: Wind toxin accumulating in the skin pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by skin redness, itching, pain, rashes or wheals. In severe cases, skin ulcer or peeling may be present. Often occurs when wind toxin retains in the skin.

Characterized by aversion to cold, cold limbs, abdominal pain with tenderness, bowel sounds, diarrhoea, loss of sense of taste with profuse salivation, and clear, profuse urine. The tongue coating is white and moist. The pulse is slow or tight. Often occurs when pathogenic cold attacks the body.

Characterized by a bright, pale complexion, cold intolerance, and clear, profuse urine. The tongue is pale with a white coating. The pulse is deep, slow or deep, thready and weak. Contributing factors may include constitutional yang qi deficiency, chronic internal dysfunctions or inappropriate treatment damaging yang qi.

Characterized by severe aversion to cold, mild fever, headache, and joint soreness/pain. The tongue coating is thin and white. The pulse is superficial and tight. Often occurs when wind cold attacks the surface of the body.

Characterized by headache, body aches, and joint pain with a cold sensation, and contracture of hands/feet. Alternatively, abdominal distension, fullness and pain with a cold sensation, vomiting of clear saliva, bowel sounds, and diarrhoea may be present. The tongue coating is white and moist. The pulse is wiry and tight. Often occurs when retained cold blocks the free flow of qi.

Characterized by cold intolerance, cold pain   that alleviates with warmth, bluish, cold limbs, delayed periods, and dysmenorrhea with dark, purple blood and clots. The tongue is dark purple with a white coating. The pulse is deep, slow  and hesitant. Often occurs when cold blocks the circulation of blood.

English_term: Retained cold dampness in the skin pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by skin numbness, stiffness, swelling, insensitivity and cold upon palpation. Often occurs when cold dampness retains in the skin.

English_term: Retained excess cold in the chest pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by pain below the heart and cold limbs. Alternatively, chest pain, abdominal distension and pain with tenderness and cough with white, thin phlegm may be present. The tongue coating is white. The pulse is deep, wiry and tight. Often occurs when pathogenic cold enters the interior or retains in the chest area due to the inappropriate use of purging therapy for Taiyang disease. It may also result from cold phlegm retention in the thoracic diaphragm.

Synonyms: Internal retention of summer heat pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by fever, thirst, dizziness, sweating, lassitude, chest tightness, and scanty, yellow urine. The tongue is red with a dry, yellow coating. The pulse is rapid. Often occurs when summer heat or pestilence attacks the body to cause a severe struggle between anti-pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors or a depletion of qi and fluids.

Synonyms: Internal retention of summer heat and dampness
English_definition_description: Characterized by alternating chills and fever, inhibited sweating, limb heaviness, thirst, restlessness, dusty complexion, chest tightness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools with a sensation of incomplete evacuation, and scanty, hesitant urination. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when summer heat and dampness or pestilence enter and remain in the body.

English_term: Summer heat and dampness obstructed spleen pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by abdominal discomfort, poor appetite, a sticky, greasy taste in the mouth, thirst with little water intake, limb soreness/heaviness/ pain, dizziness and headache with a distending sensation. Alternatively, waves of fever in the afternoon, limb oedema, loose stools, and scanty urine may be present. The tongue is pale and enlarged with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when summer heat and dampness obstruct the qi activities of the spleen and stomach.

English_term: Summer heat and dampness attacking the exterior pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by fever, mild aversion to wind cold, body heaviness, sweating/absence of sweating, and thirst. The tongue is red with a yellow coating. The pulse is soft and rapid. Often occurs when summer heat and dampness attack the surface of the body and affect the normal functioning of the Wei-defensive qi.

Characterized by persistent high fever, unconsciousness, mania, delirium, and convulsions of the limbs. Alternatively, opisthotonus and trismus may be present. Often occurs when summer heat/dampness or pestilence stir the liver wind.

Chinese_synonyms: 暑伤津气证|暑伤气津证
English_term: Summer heat consuming qi and yin pattern
Synonyms: Summer heat consuming qi and fluids pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by persistent high fever, thirst  with a desire to drink water, dry skin, lassitude, and shortness of breath. Alternatively, gastric discomfort, abdominal distension, frequent vomiting, and diarrhoea may be present. The tongue is dry and red with a dry, yellow coating. The pulse is thready and rapid. Often occurs when summer heat or pestilence consumes qi and damages yin.

Synonyms: Dampness affecting the middle jiao pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by gastric discomfort, abdominal distension, a greasy taste in the mouth, nausea, vomiting, loss of sense of taste, absence of thirst, abdominal pain, loose stools, and head/body heaviness. Alternatively, dark, yellowish eyes and body skin may be present. The tongue is pale and enlarged with a white, greasy coating. The pulse is soft and delayed. Often occurs when retained dampness impairs spleen yang.

Characterized by inhibited body fever, body heaviness, gastric discomfort, thirst with little water intake/absence of thirst, scanty, yellow urine and loose stools with a sensation of incomplete evacuation. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when damp binds with heat, resulting in difficulty clearing heat and resolving dampness.

Characterized by frequent, urgent, dribbling or painful urination. Alternatively, strong- smelling, loose stools, yellow, smelly vaginal discharge, eczema and itching of the external genitalia, and leg sores/ulcers may be present.
The tongue coating is yellow and greasy. Often occurs when damp heat flows downward to affect the intestines, urinary bladder, uterus, external genitalia, and legs.

English_term: Retained damp heat in the skin pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by skin redness, swelling, ulcers, itching, and oozing. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when damp heat affects the surface of the body.
Characterized by chronic, progressive development of ulcerative oozing that is difficult to heal. Often occurs when long-term dampness transforms into toxins.

English_term: Wind dryness attacking the exterior pattern
Synonyms: External dryness affecting the exterior pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by mild fever, aversion to wind cold, headache, absence of sweating, a dry mouth and throat, and thirst. The pulse is superficial.
Often occurs when wind dryness blocks the Wei- defensive qi and consumes body fluids.

Characterized by red, swollen, sore and ulcerative throat, constipation, dark yellow urine, thirst with a desire to drink water and dry nose and skin.
Alternatively, red, ulcerative eyes may be present. The tongue is dry. The pulse is thready and hesitant. Often occurs when toxic dry heat attacks the body.

Chinese_synonyms: 热毒炽盛证|邪热炽盛证|火热炽盛证
English_definition_description: Characterized by red, swollen, ulcerative and painful skin boils with a burning sensation, fever, and thirst. The tongue is red with a yellow coating. The pulse is rapid. Often occurs when fire heat transforms into toxins.

Characterized by persistent high fever, red face and eyes, restlessness, thirst with a desire to drink cold water, constipation and scanty, dark yellow urine. In severe cases, unconsciousness and delirium may be present. The tongue is red with a dry, yellow coating. The pulse is deep and excessive. Often occurs when external pathogenic warm heat enters the interior.

Characterized by fever, aversion to wind, headache, thirst, sore throat, and cough with yellow phlegm. Sores, ulcers or boils may also be present. The tongue coating is thin and white or slightly yellow. The pulse is superficial and rapid. Often occurs when wind, heat or summer dryness attacks the surface of the body.

Chinese_synonyms: 火毒内陷证|火毒内闭证|热毒内闭证
Synonyms: Interior fire toxin pattern|fire/heat toxin blocking the interior pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by a high-grade fever, thirst, unconsciousness, delirium, a dark red complexion, constipation and yellow urine. The tongue is dark red with a yellow coating. The pulse is deep and rapid. Often occurs when exuberant fire/heat toxins enters the zang–fu organs.

Characterized by fever, thirst with a desire to drink cold water, dry stools, and scanty, dark yellow urine. The tongue is dry and red with a dry, yellow coating. The pulse is thready and rapid. Often occurs when exuberant fire/heat damages yin fluids.

English_term: Exuberant heat affecting the chest pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by pain below the heart with tenderness, constipation, and fever or waves  of fever. Alternatively, chest or abdominal distension/pain and cough may be present. The tongue coating is yellow. The pulse is deep and
wiry. Often occurs when pathogenic factors affect the heart/chest due to inappropriate treatment of Taiyang disease. It may also occur as a result of phlegm-fluid retention in the thoracic diaphragm.

Characterized by fever, thirst with a desire to drink water, dry, withered skin, sunken eyes, dry stools, and scanty, yellow urine. The tongue is dry and red. The pulse is thready and rapid. Often occurs when exuberant fire/heat consumes or damages bodily fluids.

English_term: Warm toxin attacking the exterior pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by fever, mild aversion to cold, body aches (like being beaten with a stick), and splitting headache. The tongue is red with a yellow, white coating. The pulse is superficial and rapid. Often occurs when fire/heat or pestilence attacks the Wei-defensive exterior.

English_term: Retained heat toxin in the skin pattern
Synonyms: Fire toxin accumulating in the skin pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by red, swelling and painful skin sores/ulcers/boils with a burning sensation.
Alternatively, thirst and constipation may be present. The tongue is red with a yellow coating. The pulse is rapid. Often occurs when toxic fire heat accumulates or remains in the skin.

Characterized by red, swollen, itchy, numb or painful skin sores/boils, coupled with a burning sensation. Alternatively red, swollen and painful face, nose and eyes, fever, thirst, unconsciousness, delirium, constipation and yellow urine may be present. The tongue is deep red with brown/ yellow coating. The pulse is surging and
rapid. Often occurs when toxic wind-fire/heat accumulates in the skin.

English_term: Toxin entering the Ying- nutrients blood pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by a high fever, excessive thirst, unconsciousness, delirium and dark purple maculae or bleeding of dark red blood. The tongue is deep red. The pulse is rapid. Often occurs when toxic fire/heat enters the Ying nutrients and blood.
Characterized by a persistent low-grade fever and toxin-based symptoms. Often occurs when residual toxin remains in the body.

Characterized by sores/ulcers with the discharge of pus with a strong odour, fever and thirst. The tongue coating is putrid and greasy. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when toxic pus accumulates in the body.

English_term: Epidemic toxin blocking the heart spirit pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by unconsciousness, delirium, sound of phlegm in the throat, difficulty breathing and constipation. Often occurs when epidemic toxin blocks the heart spirit.

English_term: Pathogenic factors hidden in the pleurodiaphragmatic interspace pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by alternating chills and fever at fixed hours, a severe, splitting headache, body pain, distension and tightness in the sub-costal region, and vomiting of phlegm and saliva. The tongue coating appears like white powder. Often occurs when epidemic pathogens hide in between the exterior and interior.

Synonyms: Pattern of wind and water contending with each other
English_definition_description: Characterized by sudden oedema in the eyelids, head, face and four limbs. Alternatively, wheals, mild aversion to wind cold and scanty urine may be present. The pulse is superficial. Often occurs when external wind affects the dispersing of lung qi and results in internal water retention.

Characterized by persistent low fever or fever at night, restlessness, thirst, constipation, yellow urine, and fatigue. The tongue is dry and red. The pulse is thready and rapid. Often occurs when pathogenic heat is not completely removed.

English_term: Interior blockage and exterior collapse pattern
English_definition_description:
Characterized by fever, cough, and panting. Alternatively, tenesmus, urine retention, constipation, cardiac or abdominal colic, a pale face, cold limbs, cold sweats, and faint breathing may be present. The pulse is extremely feeble.
Often occurs when excessive pathogenic factors block the interior and anti-pathogenic qi becomes extremely deficient.

Characterized by coughing with white phlegm, chest tightness, gastric stuffiness, panting, wheezing sounds, cold intolerance, and cold limbs. The tongue coating is white and greasy. The pulse is wiry, slippery or wiry and tense. Often occurs when pathogenic cold binds with turbid phlegm.

Characterized by coughing with yellow phlegm, fever and thirst. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when turbid phlegm binds with pathogenic heat.

Characterized by cough with easy expectoration of profuse, sticky phlegm, limb heaviness, dizziness, tinnitus, chest stuffiness, and tightness, a low food intake, a greasy taste and a foreign body sensation in the throat. The tongue coating is white and greasy. The pulse is soft and slippery. Often results from the internal build up of phlegm dampness.

Characterized by vomiting of foamy phlegm, chest tightness, dizziness, headache, eye distension/ pain, sound of phlegm in the throat, and deviation of the eyes and mouth border. The tongue coating is white and greasy. The pulse is wiry and slippery. Often occurs when external wind that carries turbid phlegm attacks the body or liver wind that carries turbid phlegm affects the body.

Characterized by cough with difficult expectoration of sticky or blood-stained phlegm, chest tightness/pain, and a dry mouth and nose. The tongue is dry with a greasy coating. The pulse is hesitant. Often results from internal build up of dry heat and turbid phlegm.

Characterized by emotional depression, insomnia, dream-disturbed sleep, a foreign body sensation in the throat, fullness, and tightness in the sub- costal region and profuse phlegm. The tongue coating is white and greasy. The pulse is wiry   and slippery. Often results from phlegm binding with qi.

English_term: Phlegm qi obstructing the diaphragm pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by diaphragm fullness and tightness, a sensation of food being stuck or held up, hiccups, and vomiting of phlegm or saliva and the sensation is alleviated after belching. The tongue coating is greasy or slippery. The pulse is wiry. Often occurs when turbid phlegm obstructs the flow of qi in the diaphragm.

English_term: Phlegm and blood stasis transformed heat pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by local swelling and hardness coupled with a burning sensation and stabbing pain, chest tightness, and expectoration of yellow phlegm that may contain blood. The tongue is dark red or with ecchymosis and a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is wiry and hesitant. Often occurs when retained phlegm and blood stasis transform into heat.

English_term: Phlegm and blood stasis obstructed the diaphragm pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by diaphragm stuffiness, tightness and stabbing pain, a sensation of food being stuck or blocked, and vomiting of phlegm or saliva. The tongue is purple or with ecchymosis and a greasy coating. The pulse is hesitant. Often occurs when stagnant blood and turbid phlegm obstruct the diaphragm.

English_term: Intertwined phlegm and blood stasis pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by local lumps with stabbing pain, limb numbness or flaccidity, chest tightness,   and profuse phlegm that may contain dark  purple clots. The tongue is dark purple or with ecchymosis and a greasy coating. The pulse is wiry and hesitant. Often occurs when turbid phlegm intertwines with stagnant blood.

Characterized by restlessness, irritability, distension and tightness in the subcostal region, a burning wandering pain, coughing, panting, expectoration of yellow phlegm, fever, and thirst. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is wiry and rapid. Often occurs when phlegm heat obstructs the flow of qi.

English_term: Phlegm fire blocked the heart spirit pattern
Synonyms: Phlegm heat blocked the interior pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by fever, thirst, a red face, rapid breathing, restlessness, mania, unconsciousness, delirium, sound of phlegm in the throat, constipation and yellow urine. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when intertwined fire heat and turbid phlegm blocks the heart mind.

Characterized by distension and tightness in the subcostal region, cough, panting, fever, thirst, expectoration of yellow, sticky phlegm, sound of phlegm in the throat, convulsions of the limbs, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and wiry. Often occurs when internal phlegm heat stirs liver wind.

English_term: Phlegm heat affecting the chest pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by a feverish sensation in the chest, chest stuffiness, distension and pain, coughing with yellow phlegm, abdominal hardness and fullness with tenderness. The tongue is red with a yellow, greasy coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Often occurs when turbid phlegm and heat remain in the chest.

English_term: Intermingled phlegm and food stagnation pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by chest stuffiness, tightness, distension and pain, coughing with phlegm, a low food intake, abdominal distension, and vomiting of phlegm and undigested food. The tongue coating is putrid and greasy. The pulse is wiry and slippery. Often occurs when turbid phlegm and undigested food obstruct the flow of qi.

Characterized by painless, subcutaneous nodules on the neck and limbs. These nodules are hard, smooth and mobile. They do not appear red or feel warm. The tongue coating is greasy. The pulse is wiry and slippery. Often occurs when turbid phlegm remains in the body.

Characterized by bleeding of dark purple blood with clots, localized stabbing pain with a fixed position or bluish lumps. The tongue is purple or with ecchymosis. The pulse is hesitant. Often occurs when stagnant blood causes the blood to flow out of the vessels.

Characterized by stabbing pain with a burning sensation, bluish lumps, afternoon or night fever, and a dry mouth with no desire to drink water.
The tongue is dark red or with ecchymosis. The pulse is hesitant and rapid. Often occurs when prolonged blood stasis transforms into heat.

English_term: Blood stasis induced water retention pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by abdominal masses with a stabbing pain, abdominal bulging, inhibited urination, amenorrhoea or oedema. Alternatively, bluish, diffuse swelling and distending pain may be present. The tongue is pale purple or with ecchymosis. The pulse is hesitant. Often occurs when stagnant blood causes water retention.

English_term: Stagnant blood obstructed the diaphragm pattern
English_definition_description: Characterized by stabbing pain in the diaphragm or epigastric area with a fixed location or difficulty in swallowing food. The tongue is purple or with ecchymosis. The pulse is wiry and hesitant. Often occurs when stagnant blood retains in the thoracic diaphragm.

English_term: Fluids overflowing into the limbs pattern
